newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean 3-yr yields end at 18-month high on Sammi.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean 3-yr yields end at 18-month high on Sammi.

text.p: Yields on three-year corporates closed at a new 18-month high on Wednesday as the Sammi Group's financial crisis added further strain to the already tightening money market, brokers said.
The three-month CDs and the overnight call rate also rose due to rising money demand in the short-term money market, they said.
* 3-yr corporates end at 12.85 pct from 12.75 on Tuesday
* 3-mth CDs close at 13.55 pct from 13.20 pct
Brokers said the yields would rise further on Thursday.
Liquidity in the short-term money market remained tight because of the central bank's review on Saturday of banks' reserve status.
The three-month CDs and the overnight call rate edged up due to rising money demand in the short-term money market.
"But the release of 800 billion won from the state budget limited the rise in the call rate," Kim said.
New issues for the three-year corporates were estimated at 30.3 billion won today. On Thursday, they will be 130 billion won. --KIM MYONG-HWAN (822) 727 5645
